raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
### What does this PR do?

Makes Megatron MXFP4 QAT on MoE models about 9× cheaper per forward on the routed experts, with bit-identical results.

ModelOpt's `_QuantTEGroupedLinear` calls the weight quantizer once per expert at every forward. With verl's MXFP4 backend (the compressed-tensors QDQ that keeps QAT and the exported rollout weights bit-identical), each call launches about fifty small kernels from Python. QAT on the grouped experts is therefore launch-bound. On Qwen3-30B-A3B at TP2 × EP2 (64 local experts per rank):

- In one GRPO step on 4×B300 with `qat.mode=mxfp4` (the example from #8186), `old_log_prob` took 1015 s, against 105 s for `ref`, the same model's forward without QAT. `update_actor` took 2423 s.
- One layer on one GPU at the same per-rank shapes (20,480 tokens) took 147 ms per QAT forward, against 7 ms without QAT. The GPU was busy for 25 ms of it.

The MXFP4 QDQ forms each 32-element group within one row of one weight, so quantizing the stacked expert weights gives the same values bit for bit. Under QAT, the grouped linear functional now stacks the expert weights and quantizes them in one call. It then hands the results to ModelOpt's own functional, which still quantizes the input and calls TE. Weight quantizers on other backends (FP8 block, NVFP4, ModelOpt's own formats) keep ModelOpt's per-expert loop.

The change replaces `_quantized_linear_fn` on ModelOpt's private `_QuantTEGroupedLinear` class at QAT setup, with a warning if that attribute is missing. The long-term home for batching grouped weights is ModelOpt itself; I can open an issue there if that's preferred.

### Checklist Before Starting

- [x] Search for similar PRs: none touches ModelOpt's grouped linear quantization or QAT speed (searched `QAT slow`, `grouped linear quant`, `_QuantTEGroupedLinear`, `weight_quantizer expert`).
- [x] Format the PR title as `[{modules}] {type}: {description}`.

### Test

`tests/utils/test_modelopt_grouped_weight_qdq_on_cpu.py` (new, CPU), 5 tests:

- Stacked and per-expert QDQ agree bit for bit, straight-through gradients included. The weights span 1e-3 to 30 and include an all-zero row and a group at the largest E2M1 value.
- The order of stacked and per-expert calls doesn't matter.
- The grouped functional calls the weight quantizer once on `[num_gemms, out, in]`, passes the biases through and quantizes the input once.
- Other weight backends keep the per-expert loop.
- The patch is applied once.

```bash
python -m pytest -q tests/utils/test_modelopt_grouped_weight_qdq_on_cpu.py tests/utils/test_mxfp8_ignored_layers_on_cpu.py \
  tests/utils/test_vllm_mxfp4_restage_on_cpu.py tests/utils/test_vllm_unquant_utils_on_cpu.py \
  tests/workers/test_engine_*_on_cpu.py tests/workers/test_megatron_*_on_cpu.py
# 83 passed
pre-commit run --files <changed files>   # all hooks pass
bash scripts/generate_trainer_config.sh  # All good
```

GPU, one B300, one Qwen3-30B-A3B layer on the Transformer Engine spec. Per-rank shapes at TP2 × EP2: 64 experts, expert FFN 384, hidden 2048. 20,480 tokens, warm iterations. Same layer instance before and after the change:

| | Per expert (before) | Batched (this PR) |
|---|---|---|
| weight-quantizer calls per forward | 128 | 2 |
| forward (ms) | 139.0 | 15.4 |
| forward + backward (ms) | 168.2 | 33.7 |
| peak memory, forward / forward + backward (GB) | 4.8 / 7.0 | 5.8 / 7.6 |
| without QAT, forward / forward + backward (ms) | 7.0 / 26.3 | |

Bit-identity on the GPU:

- QDQ of the layer's real expert weights and of random weights (1e-4 to 50) is equal stacked and per expert.
- The layer's forward is not deterministic by default: two runs before the change already differ. With Megatron `deterministic_mode`, `CUBLAS_WORKSPACE_CONFIG=:4096:8` and `NVTE_ALLOW_NONDETERMINISTIC_ALGO=0`, two runs before the change are identical. Against them, this PR gives bit-identical no-grad outputs, grad-mode outputs, input gradients and all parameter gradients.

End to end, the MXFP4 recipe in #8426 (Qwen3-30B-A3B GRPO, 4×B300, TP2 × EP2, `qat.mode=mxfp4`):

- First step on the same four GPUs: 3743 s on main 174888fc, 1056 s on main 2ab35292 with this change (the commits in between change the rollout's request gate, DeepSeek-V4 and ROCm guards and tracing, not the training path). By phase: `old_log_prob` 1015 → 179 s, `update_actor` 2423 → 569 s, `ref` 105 s in both; `rollout_corr/kl` 0.0030 in both.
- Ten steps per arm with this change: 1031 s per step with QAT, against 890 s for the MXFP4 rollout without QAT and 829 s in BF16; `rollout_corr/kl` 0.0031, 0.0142 and 0.0017.

### Design & Code Changes

- `verl/utils/qat/modelopt.py`: `_batch_grouped_expert_weight_qdq()`, called from `apply_qat`, wraps `_QuantTEGroupedLinear._quantized_linear_fn`. When the weight quantizer is enabled on verl's MXFP4 backend and the expert weights share shape, dtype and device, it quantizes `torch.stack(weights)` once. It then calls ModelOpt's original functional through a view of the module whose `weight_quantizer` is the identity. Every other case calls the original unchanged.
- `tests/utils/test_modelopt_grouped_weight_qdq_on_cpu.py`: new CPU test.

### Checklist Before Submitting

- [x] Read the [Contribute Guide](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
- [x] Apply pre-commit checks.
- [ ] Add / Update the documentation: no user-facing change.
- [x] Add unit tests (CPU).

AI assistance was used for this change. I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests above.

@@ -0,0 +1,153 @@
+# Copyright 2026 Bytedance Ltd. and/or its affiliates
+#
+# Licensed under the Apache License, Version 2.0 (the "License");
+# you may not use this file except in compliance with the License.
+# You may obtain a copy of the License at
+#
+# http://www.apache.org/licenses/LICENSE-2.0
+#
+# Unless required by applicable law or agreed to in writing, software
+# distributed under the License is distributed on an "AS IS" BASIS,
+# WITHOUT WARRANTIES OR CONDITIONS OF ANY KIND, either express or implied.
+# See the License for the specific language governing permissions and
+# limitations under the License.
+
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+import torch.nn as nn
+
+pytest.importorskip("compressed_tensors")
+pytest.importorskip("modelopt")
+pytest.importorskip("transformer_engine")
+
+# Hide an unusable optional FlashAttention-4 package before ModelOpt imports Megatron.
+# isort: off
+import verl.models.mcore  # noqa: F401
+import modelopt.torch.quantization as mtq
+from modelopt.torch.quantization.plugins.transformer_engine import _QuantTEGroupedLinear
+from verl.utils.qat.modelopt import _batch_grouped_expert_weight_qdq, build_quantize_config
+
+# isort: on
+
+NUM_GEMMS = 4
+
+
+def _expert_weight_quantizer(qat_mode):
+    """The routed-expert weight quantizer ModelOpt builds for ``qat_mode``."""
+    model = nn.Module()
+    model.mlp = nn.Module()
+    model.mlp.experts = nn.Module()
+    model.mlp.experts.linear_fc1 = nn.Linear(256, 64, bias=False, dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+    mtq.quantize(model, build_quantize_config(qat_mode))
+    return model.mlp.experts.linear_fc1.weight_quantizer
+
+
+def _expert_weights():
+    torch.manual_seed(0)
+    weights = [torch.randn(64, 256, dtype=torch.bfloat16) * scale for scale in (1e-3, 0.05, 1.0, 30.0)]
+    weights[1][3] = 0  # an all-zero row
+    weights[2][5, :32] = 6.0  # a group sitting on the largest E2M1 value
+    return weights
+
+
+class _Recorder:
+    """An enabled pass-through quantizer that records the shapes it sees (the MXFP8 input quantizer needs CUDA)."""
+
+    is_enabled = True
+
+    def __init__(self, backend=None):
+        self.backend = backend
+        self.calls = []
+
+    def __call__(self, tensor):
+        self.calls.append(tensor.shape)
+        return tensor
+
+
+def _count_calls(module):
+    calls = []
+    module.register_forward_hook(lambda mod, inputs, output: calls.append(inputs[0].shape))
+    return calls
+
+
+def _grouped_call(weight_quantizer, input_quantizer, weights):
+    """Run the (patched) grouped linear functional on TE's _GroupedLinear.apply argument layout."""
+    _batch_grouped_expert_weight_qdq()
+    seen = {}
+
+    def apply(inp, non_tensor_args, *weights_and_biases):
+        seen["inp"], seen["weights_and_biases"] = inp, weights_and_biases
+        return inp
+
+    module = SimpleNamespace(
+        num_gemms=NUM_GEMMS,
+        input_quantizer=input_quantizer,
+        weight_quantizer=weight_quantizer,
+        output_quantizer=nn.Identity(),
+    )
+    inp = torch.randn(8, 256, dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+    biases = [torch.zeros(64, dtype=torch.bfloat16) for _ in range(NUM_GEMMS)]
+    non_tensor_args = ([2] * NUM_GEMMS,)
+    _QuantTEGroupedLinear._quantized_linear_fn(
+        SimpleNamespace(_apply=apply), "_apply", module, inp, non_tensor_args, *weights, *biases
+    )
+    return seen, biases
+
+
+def test_stacked_mxfp4_weight_qdq_matches_per_expert():
+    weight_quantizer = _expert_weight_quantizer("mxfp4")
+    weights = [w.requires_grad_(True) for w in _expert_weights()]
+    per_expert = torch.stack([weight_quantizer(w) for w in weights])
+    stacked = weight_quantizer(torch.stack(weights))
+    assert torch.equal(per_expert, stacked)
+
+    # the straight-through gradient reaches every expert weight unchanged
+    upstream = torch.randn_like(stacked)
+    grads_loop = torch.autograd.grad((per_expert * upstream).sum(), weights)
+    grads_stacked = torch.autograd.grad((weight_quantizer(torch.stack(weights)) * upstream).sum(), weights)
+    for g_loop, g_stacked, g_ref in zip(grads_loop, grads_stacked, upstream.unbind(0), strict=True):
+        assert torch.equal(g_loop, g_stacked)
+        assert torch.equal(g_stacked, g_ref)
+
+
+def test_stacked_call_leaves_the_quantizer_unchanged_for_single_experts():
+    # TensorQuantizer derives some state from the input's rank; a stacked call first must not change later 2-D calls
+    weight_quantizer = _expert_weight_quantizer("mxfp4")
+    weights = _expert_weights()
+    stacked = weight_quantizer(torch.stack(weights))
+    per_expert = torch.stack([weight_quantizer(w) for w in weights])
+    assert torch.equal(stacked, per_expert)
+    assert torch.equal(weight_quantizer(torch.stack(weights)), stacked)
+
+
+def test_mxfp4_grouped_linear_quantizes_all_experts_in_one_call():
+    weight_quantizer, input_quantizer = _expert_weight_quantizer("mxfp4"), _Recorder()
+    weights = _expert_weights()
+    expected = [weight_quantizer(w) for w in weights]
+    weight_calls = _count_calls(weight_quantizer)
+
+    seen, biases = _grouped_call(weight_quantizer, input_quantizer, weights)
+
+    assert weight_calls == [torch.Size([NUM_GEMMS, 64, 256])]
+    assert input_quantizer.calls == [torch.Size([8, 256])]
+    quantized, passed_biases = seen["weights_and_biases"][:NUM_GEMMS], seen["weights_and_biases"][NUM_GEMMS:]
+    for got, want in zip(quantized, expected, strict=True):
+        assert torch.equal(got, want)
+    assert all(got is want for got, want in zip(passed_biases, biases, strict=True))
+
+
+def test_other_weight_backends_keep_the_per_expert_loop():
+    weight_quantizer = _Recorder(backend="verl_fp8_block")
+
+    _grouped_call(weight_quantizer, _Recorder(), _expert_weights())
+
+    assert weight_quantizer.calls == [torch.Size([64, 256])] * NUM_GEMMS
+
+
+def test_patch_is_applied_once():
+    _batch_grouped_expert_weight_qdq()
+    patched = _QuantTEGroupedLinear.__dict__["_quantized_linear_fn"]
+    _batch_grouped_expert_weight_qdq()
+    assert _QuantTEGroupedLinear.__dict__["_quantized_linear_fn"] is patched

     return {"quant_cfg": quant_cfg, "algorithm": algorithm}
 
 
+class _QuantizedWeightsView:
+    """The grouped linear module as ModelOpt's functional sees it, with the expert weights already quantized."""
+
+    def __init__(self, module: nn.Module):
+        self._module = module
+
+    def __getattr__(self, name):
+        return getattr(self._module, name)
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def weight_quantizer(weight: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+        return weight
+
+
+def _batch_grouped_expert_weight_qdq() -> None:
+    """Fake-quantize all expert weights of a TE grouped linear in one quantizer call.
+
+    ModelOpt's ``_QuantTEGroupedLinear`` calls its weight quantizer once per expert at every forward. With MXFP4
+    that is about fifty small kernels per expert, launched from Python: on Qwen3-30B-A3B at TP2 x EP2 (64 local
+    experts), a QAT forward of one layer took 147 ms against 7 ms without QAT, with the GPU idle most of the time.
+    The MXFP4 QDQ forms each 32-element group within a row of one weight, so quantizing the stacked weights gives
+    the same values, bit for bit, as quantizing them one by one. Other weight backends keep ModelOpt's per-expert
+    loop.
+    """
+    try:
+        from modelopt.torch.quantization.plugins.transformer_engine import _QuantTEGroupedLinear
+    except ImportError:
+        return
+
+    original = _QuantTEGroupedLinear.__dict__.get("_quantized_linear_fn")
+    original_fn = getattr(original, "__func__", original)
+    if original_fn is None:
+        logger.warning(
+            "ModelOpt's _QuantTEGroupedLinear has no _quantized_linear_fn; MXFP4 expert weights stay per expert"
+        )
+        return
+    if getattr(original_fn, "_verl_batched_weight_qdq", False):
+        return
+
+    def quantized_linear_fn(package, func_name, self, *args):
+        quantizer = self.weight_quantizer
+        num_gemms = getattr(self, "num_gemms", 0)
+        batchable = getattr(quantizer, "is_enabled", False) and getattr(quantizer, "backend", None) == _MXFP4_BACKEND
+        if not batchable or num_gemms < 2 or 2 * num_gemms > len(args):
+            return original_fn(package, func_name, self, *args)
+        # *weights_and_biases is the trailing variadic of TE's _GroupedLinear: num_gemms weights, then num_gemms biases
+        start = len(args) - 2 * num_gemms
+        weights = args[start : start + num_gemms]
+        if len({(w.shape, w.dtype, w.device) for w in weights}) != 1:
+            return original_fn(package, func_name, self, *args)
+        quantized = quantizer(torch.stack(weights)).unbind(0)
+        args = (*args[:start], *quantized, *args[start + num_gemms :])
+        return original_fn(package, func_name, _QuantizedWeightsView(self), *args)
+
+    quantized_linear_fn._verl_batched_weight_qdq = True
+    _QuantTEGroupedLinear._quantized_linear_fn = staticmethod(quantized_linear_fn)
+    logger.info("QAT: TE grouped linears fake-quantize their MXFP4 expert weights in one call")
+
+
 def apply_qat(
     model: nn.Module,
     qat_mode: str,
     ignore_patterns: list[str] | None = None,
 ) -> nn.Module:
     """Apply Quantization-Aware Training to a Megatron model."""
     config = build_quantize_config(qat_mode, ignore_patterns)
+    _batch_grouped_expert_weight_qdq()
     mtq.quantize(model, config)
     return model
